questions.prompt: The window is 128,000 tokens, maxOutput is 8,000 and headroom is 16,000, with a ratio of 0.8. What is the threshold?
questions.explanation: 128,000 x 0.8 is 102,400 and 128,000 - 8,000 - 16,000 is 104,000. The threshold is the smaller of the two, 102,400.

questions.prompt: Why does measure use the provider's exact usage for the last request and estimate only what was added since?
options: The exact count exists only after a request, so newer messages must be estimated
Estimates are always more accurate than usage
The provider charges extra for counting tokens
Usage counts only the system prompt
questions.explanation: The provider reports exact tokens for a request it has already processed. Messages added after it have not been sent yet, so their size is estimated, about four characters per token.

questions.prompt: measure is 102,900 and the window is 128,000. Why act now when 25,100 tokens are still free?
options: Because the provider rejects any request above 100,000 tokens
Because the threshold reserves room for the reply and for the work of shrinking history, and estimates can be wrong
Because reuse of the prefix stops above the threshold
Because the system prompt must be resent
questions.explanation: The free space is the reserve. Acting at the threshold leaves room for the reply and for later work instead of failing mid-task.
